newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Sexual equality stops in barber's chair.
newsitem.headline: Sexual equality stops in barber's chair.

text.p: An Australian air force corporal who wanted long hair like his female colleagues lost an equal opportunity case on Wednesday after a tribunal ruled that military crewcuts for men were not discriminatory.
Carl Trindorfer, 25, had argued that the compulsory short back and sides haircut for male recruits was unfair.
Trindorfer, an avionics fitter with the Royal Australian Air Force, had told the commission that having long hair would not change the way he worked or affect discipline.
But an Australian state equal opportunity commission decided different grooming rules for men and women were not a problem.
"It is differential treatment...but it is not discriminatory," ruled commissioner John Nader.
"The uniformity of appearance of the members of various units of the defence force is a legitimate objective," he said.
